votes.reason: JNJ is a sound business with trailing EPS up 8.6%, and although 25.3x after a 14.8% 12-week run to a 52-week high makes it fully priced rather than cheap, a thin margin of safety on a quality defensive is not a concrete value case against holding it this week.

CVX is sound, with trailing EPS up 27.2% at 19.2x, a fair multiple for that growth, and my caution about buying energy with crude at $91 is why I did not pick it, not a concrete case against the business this week.
PGR is the cheapest sound business in the draft at 11.6x trailing with EPS still growing 10.1%, so the value case that put it in the book still holds.

At 19.4x trailing after a Q2 beat, LMT is a fair price for a sound defense prime even though much of its 52.8% EPS growth is recovery from earlier program charges, and its 10% four-week slide came on yields rather than the business.

At 34.2x trailing, the draft's highest multiple by almost nine turns, CAT is priced like a growth stock on cyclical heavy-machinery earnings, so its 10.45% 12-week slide has bought no margin of safety, and a hot CPI on Friday would hit the book's richest valuation hardest.
